title: 5D-STEM for Soft Matter: Mapping Polymer Morphology and Crystallinity in 3D
content: Polyolefins are among the most widely produced and utilized polymers, playing a central role in packaging, construction, textiles, and other applications. Despite their ubiquity, their inherent immiscibility and phase separation challenge both mechanical performance and recyclability, particularly in mixed plastic waste streams. Recent studies have shown that dynamic covalent crosslinking can stabilize co-continuous polyolefin blends, improving both their mechanical properties and processability [1]. However, a detailed 3D structural understanding of polyolefin blends, including phase distribution, crystallinity, and orientation, remains limited due to their semicrystalline nature and susceptibility to beam damage in conventional electron microscopy.
